newsitem.title: FINLAND: SCANT IMPACT SEEN FROM VANHALA REMARKS - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: SCANT IMPACT SEEN FROM VANHALA REMARKS - ANALYSTS.

text.p: Bank of Finland board member Matti Vanhala's remarks on Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) on Wednesday were not expected to move Finnish financial markets on Thursday, analysts said.

Vanhala said the finance ministry's austere budget plans were inflation neutral and that he assumed that the ERM central parity rate would be a fair and likely euro conversion rate, but there was nothing surprising in his comments, they said.
"This was pretty much the kind of talk that had been expected," said Merita analyst Jukka Lepomaki.
"Based on this there will be no reaction," he added.
But he said he disagreed with Vanhala's comments that nothing would have changed fundamentally since the markka was linked to the ERM, and noted that the dollar has strengthened 20 percent this year.
He also disagreed with Vanhala's view that there was still spare capacity in many sectors where growth was spreading.
The remarks came after the Finnish interbank bond market had closed for the day.

OKOBANK Treasury economist Teppo Koivisto agreed that Vanhala said nothing surprising but said his comments about the role of the autumn incomes settlement talks supported a view that the central bank would hold rates until after the talks.
"That soothed money markets a little," he said.
He also said there was a slight rise in DEM/FIM after Vanhala advocated the ERM central parity rate as a euro conversion rate if Finland joins EMU.
Enskilda's Esko Torsti took the opposite view:
"I think the yield curve will flatten somewhat and DEM/FIM come down," he said.

Torsti said he interpreted Vanhala's comments as a second warning about monetary policy tightening and that since Finnish FRAs have been steady in recent days while German rates have been restless, especially the June FRA rate could rise.
"It showed clearly that the Bank of Finland has put its finger to the trigger but is hesitating," he said.
